title: Macrophage-derived features predict thyroid cancer lymph-node status in retrospective cohorts
summary: Machine-learning combinations using SPP1-positive macrophage-derived molecular features classified lymph-node status in papillary thyroid cancer cohorts. The selected glmBoost/random-forest model had AUC 0.998 in training, 0.706 in held-out TCGA data and 0.657 in a combined GEO cohort. Those latter cohorts contributed to model prioritization, so the results are cross-cohort assessments rather than untouched external validation. Single-cell discovery involved three patients. Separate cell and small mouse experiments supported SPP1 as a therapeutic candidate; they do not validate clinical prediction or establish a human treatment benefit.
ai_technology: glmBoost and random forest; 111 combinations of 12 learned model strategies
organization: Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine; Lanzhou University; Central South University; Zhengzhou University; Soochow University; Medical University of Graz; German Cancer Research Center; Nanjing Medical University; Charité – Universitätsmedizin Berlin; Chongqing University; Chongqing Medical University

evidence.tested: Patient-level 70/30 TCGA partition; features selected in training and 111 model combinations compared. Selected model AUCs were 0.998/0.706/0.657 across training, held-out TCGA and Meta-PTC. Meta-PTC includes 21 pN0 and 50 pN1 tumors; model prioritization used held-out/meta-cohort performance.
evidence.unknown: The three-patient single-cell discovery cohort and model-selection use of evaluation cohorts limit generalization. Prospective clinical benefit is unestablished. Separate SPP1-inhibitor cell and mouse experiments are ancillary preclinical evidence, not validation of a frozen clinical predictor.
evidence.ai_role: Learned model combinations use macrophage-associated expression features to classify nodal status; glmBoost/random forest was selected through cross-cohort comparison. The represented claim is this clinical cohort result, not an autonomous AI discovery of SPP1 biology.

source_review.scope: Full source-provenanced publisher HTML text independently read: study data/cohorts, learned-model Methods, relevant Results, experimental limits, affiliation and publication metadata. No underlying data reanalysis or supplementary-figure validation.
